sources.title: Harness Ultragoal final review and implementation-handoff mission
verified_facts: The requested product includes the plugin, Rust CLI, Harness-owned tools, installation/discovery, fitting, observability, journeys, research, proof, release, and completion authority.
binding_product_requirements: All explicit mission, review-standard, handoff, deliverable, quality-gate, and claim-ceiling constraints in the request.
sources.limitations: Defines desired product and review authority, not live implementation evidence.

sources.title: Harness Ultragoal Sol Pro Review Snapshot 00-READ-ME-FIRST
verified_facts: The package declares itself a snapshot and expressly disclaims live installation, cache, app-registry, release, and runtime proof.
binding_product_requirements: Treat all snapshot state as context, not live proof; preserve the stated claim ceiling.
sources.limitations: Its own file is outside a supplied archive-wide digest manifest; the review computed its digest independently.

sources.title: Verified repository snapshot and tracked source digest set
sources.publisher: Snapshot producer; independently checked in this review
verified_facts: All 5,011 tracked source digests and all 3,499 fixture digests match the supplied manifests; the candidate content-set digest also matches.
binding_product_requirements: Use repository findings as migration/implementation input only; recompute live state before implementation.
sources.limitations: The archive has 249 copied metadata/evidence/research/legacy files not covered by a supplied archive-wide digest manifest and cannot prove the current branch or runtime.

sources.title: Sol Extra High successor contract candidate v1
verified_facts: The 17 candidate files match their supplied per-entry and content-set digests.
advisory_practices: Plugin-first framing, truth-surface separation, adaptive orchestration, explicit custom-tool necessity, and strict claim boundaries were retained after falsification.
rejected_recommendations: Binding status conditioned on completed validators/proof
Twenty-four top-level laws
Nineteen separately authoritative custom tools
Host-internal proof requirements without capability ceilings
sources.limitations: A coherent candidate is not live product or contract adoption proof.

sources.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
verified_facts: GPT-5.6 is generally available; Sol is the flagship; Ultra is described as the highest-capability setting coordinating multiple agents.
binding_product_requirements: Do not hard-code stale predecessor model names as product law; record actual runtime metadata when exposed.
advisory_practices: Use multi-agent work only when workstreams divide cleanly.
experimental_hypotheses: Ultra orchestration can reduce wall-clock time for cleanly separable work; validate on this repository.
rejected_recommendations: Adopting vendor benchmark scores as product completion criteria
sources.limitations: Product announcement; does not expose or prove the later local Codex runtime configuration.

sources.title: Model guidance for GPT-5.6
verified_facts: Pro mode is configured with reasoning.mode=pro independently from reasoning effort; persisted reasoning, explicit prompt caching, programmatic tool calling, and multi-agent features have distinct contracts.
binding_product_requirements: Never infer model/mode from prompt text; treat runtime metadata as an observed surface with a bounded claim.
advisory_practices: Use the smallest prompt/tool set that reliably works
Benchmark migration on representative tasks
Use programmatic tool calling only for bounded tool-heavy processing
experimental_hypotheses: Persisted reasoning or prompt caching may improve efficiency without changing product authority; measure before adoption.
rejected_recommendations: Treating persisted reasoning as repository state or proof
Making programmatic tool calling a universal orchestration layer
sources.limitations: API feature availability may differ from the local Codex host and must be capability-probed.

sources.title: Follow a goal
verified_facts: /goal attaches a durable objective; effective goals define the target, constraints, validation loop, and stopping condition and can be paused, resumed, or cleared.
binding_product_requirements: The implementation handoff states outcome, constraints, validation, stopping conditions, recovery, and keeps host goal state separate from product state.
advisory_practices: Use checkpoints and compact progress reports.
rejected_recommendations: Creating a competing repository goal engine
sources.limitations: Host support and runtime state must be observed in the actual project.

sources.title: Developer commands: /goal
verified_facts: A /goal objective must be non-empty and at most 4,000 characters; longer instructions should live in a file referenced by the objective.
binding_product_requirements: The exact handoff begins with /goal, remains within 4,000 characters, and obtains detailed authority through verified local files rather than hidden chat context.
advisory_practices: Keep the objective compact and file-referential.
rejected_recommendations: Embedding the full successor contract in the /goal objective
sources.limitations: The documented limit does not prove that Goal mode is enabled in the later local project.

sources.title: Plugins overview
verified_facts: Plugins package skills and optional app/MCP capabilities; installation is followed by a new session/chat; hooks require review and trust.
binding_product_requirements: Use supported plugin components and prove source, install, discovery, and runtime separately; hooks cannot be essential to correctness without explicit trust.
advisory_practices: Test installed plugins in a new task.
rejected_recommendations: Assuming install automatically proves discovery
Using untrusted hooks as a mandatory enforcement path
sources.limitations: Host UI and capabilities can vary by version and account.

sources.title: Build plugins
verified_facts: A plugin requires .codex-plugin/plugin.json; repo marketplaces use $REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json and personal marketplaces use ~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json; local source paths are relative and ./-prefixed.
binding_product_requirements: Implement and verify supported repo/personal marketplace wiring, required manifest paths, stable package inventory, and new-task discovery.
advisory_practices: Use plugin creator tooling as scaffolding, not authority.
rejected_recommendations: Treating plugin-manifest-draft.json resources as host runtime wiring
sources.limitations: Exact host registry APIs remain capability-dependent.

sources.title: Build skills
verified_facts: Skills are reusable workflows and use progressive disclosure; SKILL.md requires name and description metadata.
binding_product_requirements: Every shipped skill has valid metadata, accurate trigger descriptions, bounded references, and one product-semantic owner.
advisory_practices: Keep long references and scripts outside the initial metadata context.
rejected_recommendations: A large overlapping skill set with multiple front doors
sources.limitations: Metadata validity alone does not prove skill selection or behavior.

sources.title: Subagents and custom agents
verified_facts: Custom agents are defined under ~/.codex/agents or .codex/agents; read-only sandbox overrides are supported; parallel agents are useful for independent work and consume additional resources.
binding_product_requirements: Reconnaissance, research verification, and adversarial review agents are read-only; write work is delegated only with explicit disjoint scope and root acceptance.
advisory_practices: Use built-in explorer/worker roles where sufficient and keep subagent prompts bounded.
experimental_hypotheses: Run-scoped write leases outperform static write-privileged custom roles; validate through conflict/recovery trials.
rejected_recommendations: Parallel write agents on shared authority surfaces
Hard-pinning model names without runtime need
sources.limitations: Parent live permission overrides and host version still govern effective behavior.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
verified_facts: Codex layers global and repository instructions and supports nested overrides; instruction discovery must be verified from the working directory in a new run.
binding_product_requirements: Repository fitting must create/reconcile concise root guidance and scoped overrides without duplicating the full contract.
advisory_practices: Place specialized instructions close to their scope.
rejected_recommendations: Using AGENTS.md as a mutable state store or full contract dump
sources.limitations: Instruction discovery depends on actual start directory and host behavior.

sources.title: Codex worktrees
verified_facts: Worktrees isolate independent tasks in a project; concurrent tasks should not silently share writes.
binding_product_requirements: Use separate worktrees/branches for write workers when supported and still enforce semantic, not merely path, ownership.
advisory_practices: Use local mode for integration and isolated worktrees for independent implementation.
rejected_recommendations: Assuming worktrees alone prevent semantic or generated-output conflicts
sources.limitations: Worktree availability and setup behavior must be checked live.

sources.title: Codex local environments
verified_facts: Local environment setup and actions are stored under the project .codex folder and can configure worktree setup and common commands.
binding_product_requirements: Fit and migration must reconcile .codex environment setup/actions as a capability-probed product surface, not assume universal host support.
advisory_practices: Use setup scripts for checked-out worktrees and actions for common commands.
rejected_recommendations: Making app-only local environment actions the sole CLI/product entry
sources.limitations: Documented as desktop-app-only and therefore optional for CLI-only hosts.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
verified_facts: Agent legibility requires relevant product and engineering context to be discoverable in the repository; observability can be exposed to agents locally.
binding_product_requirements: Make product semantics, commands, owners, diagnostics, and validation discoverable to a fresh agent without relying on hidden chat context.
advisory_practices: Keep generated knowledge organized and queryable rather than adding ad-hoc prompt volume.
experimental_hypotheses: A compact semantic index plus generated inventories will improve fresh-agent task success; evaluate.
rejected_recommendations: Copying an external team’s exact stack or assuming their observability substrate is universally required
sources.limitations: Case study, not a universal product specification.

sources.title: An open-source spec for Codex orchestration: Symphony
verified_facts: Continuous agent orchestration benefits from an explicit control plane, agent-friendly repository, tests, and guardrails.
binding_product_requirements: Harness Ultragoal must own an explicit live work/claim graph and recovery model rather than rely on static lane files.
advisory_practices: Use external project management only as an adapter if adopted.
experimental_hypotheses: A repository-local semantic work graph is sufficient for this product without introducing an external board dependency.
rejected_recommendations: Requiring Linear or continuous unattended agents for product correctness
sources.limitations: Case study and orchestration specification; external control-plane assumptions are not adopted.

sources.title: Programmatic Tool Calling
verified_facts: Programmatic tool calling is intended for bounded tool-heavy processing with explicit allowed callers and structured outputs.
advisory_practices: Consider it for bounded filtering, joining, validation, and aggregation stages only after direct tooling works.
experimental_hypotheses: It may accelerate research/source reconciliation or large inventory checks if the local runtime exposes it.
rejected_recommendations: Using it for stages requiring fresh judgment or as a hidden universal controller
sources.limitations: API feature, not guaranteed in the local Codex project.

sources.title: Prompt caching
verified_facts: Prompt caching rewards reusable exact prefixes and is an efficiency mechanism, not application state.
advisory_practices: Keep stable contract/index prefixes concise and place variable live context later when API callers are implemented.
experimental_hypotheses: Progressive disclosure and stable prefixes may reduce latency/cost; measure representative workloads.
rejected_recommendations: Treating cache hits as correctness, persistence, or product proof
sources.limitations: Not necessarily visible or controllable in Codex host interactions.

sources.title: Reasoning and conversation state
verified_facts: Persisted reasoning can make compatible prior reasoning available across supported API calls; it is distinct from visible conversation and application state.
binding_product_requirements: No completion, current-state, or audit authority may depend on hidden/persisted reasoning.
advisory_practices: Use persisted reasoning only as an optional efficiency/quality feature in API adapters.
rejected_recommendations: Using hidden reasoning as durable product memory, provenance, or evidence
sources.limitations: Feature support and retention semantics vary by API/runtime.

sources.title: Evaluate agent workflows
verified_facts: End-to-end traces can expose model calls, tool calls, guardrails, and handoffs; trace grading can identify workflow-level failures.
binding_product_requirements: Evaluation must inspect end-to-end behavior and artifacts, preserve reproducibility, and keep vendor traces as observations rather than claim authority.
advisory_practices: Use trace grading to diagnose routing/tool/handoff failures when available.
experimental_hypotheses: Trace-derived failure harvesting will improve journey eval coverage after independent triage.
rejected_recommendations: Treating grader output as self-sufficient proof
sources.limitations: Vendor trace APIs are optional adapters and may have retention/privacy constraints.

sources.title: How we monitor internal coding agents for misalignment
verified_facts: Coding agents can optimize evaluation signals by editing or disabling tests instead of solving the underlying task.
binding_product_requirements: Tests, fixtures, receipts, telemetry, and generated rows never substitute for behavior; proof must include tamper/reward-hacking controls and protected authority surfaces.
advisory_practices: Use independent diff/reviewer checks for validation-surface changes.
rejected_recommendations: Allowing implementation workers to own acceptance tests and final claim authority without review
sources.limitations: Risk evidence supports controls but does not quantify this repository’s incidence.

sources.title: Evaluation best practices and Evals platform transition
verified_facts: Generative systems require evaluations; the legacy Evals platform has a stated read-only and shutdown transition in late 2026.
binding_product_requirements: Harness-owned evaluation semantics and stored results must be vendor-neutral; deprecated vendor surfaces cannot be product authority.
advisory_practices: Use current supported APIs/adapters when selected.
rejected_recommendations: Binding the product contract to a deprecated hosted Evals platform
sources.limitations: The deprecation timeline may change and must be rechecked before implementation decisions.

sources.title: cargo check
verified_facts: cargo check is faster because it skips final code generation, and therefore cannot report some code-generation diagnostics.
binding_product_requirements: Routine check may use cargo check but strict claims that depend on build/codegen behavior must run the appropriate stronger command.
advisory_practices: Exploit Cargo metadata reuse for routine iteration.
rejected_recommendations: Treating cargo check as universal build/runtime proof
sources.limitations: Command suitability depends on crate targets/features/platforms.

sources.title: cargo test
verified_facts: cargo test compiles and executes unit, integration, and documentation tests subject to target/filter configuration.
binding_product_requirements: Test claims must name selected packages, targets, features, filters, platform, and candidate identity; a zero exit code cannot imply unselected behavior.
advisory_practices: Use targeted tests in routine mode and declared complete selections in strict mode.
rejected_recommendations: Counting test files or receipts as behavior coverage
sources.limitations: Tests can be incomplete, incorrect, flaky, or reward-hacked.

sources.title: clap derive parser documentation
verified_facts: clap supports typed derive-based parsers, subcommands, and enum value parsing.
binding_product_requirements: Replace the handwritten public parser with a mature typed parser unless live implementation evidence demonstrates a superior supported alternative.
advisory_practices: Generate help and shell completions from the same command model.
rejected_recommendations: Maintaining duplicate handwritten grammar and domain validation
sources.limitations: Library choice remains an implementation decision if equivalent requirements are met.

sources.title: cargo-nextest documentation
verified_facts: Nextest supports retries/flaky classification, recording/rerun, archives, sharding, configuration profiles, and JUnit output.
advisory_practices: Use as an optional execution substrate where it materially improves isolation, reruns, or CI partitioning.
experimental_hypotheses: Recorded runs may improve failure diagnosis and impacted-test validation when bound to candidate identity.
rejected_recommendations: Making Nextest availability a prerequisite for routine correctness or giving its output Harness claim authority
sources.limitations: Third-party tool; version/features and installation must be capability-probed.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry handling sensitive data
verified_facts: Telemetry should follow data minimization, avoid unnecessary personal data, and review/redact sensitive attributes.
binding_product_requirements: Events carry privacy classes; persisted/exported data is minimized and redacted; export requires explicit configuration/consent and retention policy.
advisory_practices: Prefer aggregation or anonymization when it serves the diagnostic purpose.
rejected_recommendations: Capturing raw prompts, secrets, full paths, or unrestricted stdout by default
sources.limitations: Legal obligations depend on deployment context and require human policy decisions.

sources.title: SLSA provenance v1
verified_facts: Provenance describes how an artifact was produced so consumers can verify it against expectations and optionally rebuild it.
binding_product_requirements: Release/package provenance identifies output digests, source/candidate inputs, build process, and environment sufficiently for expectation-based verification.
advisory_practices: Use standard provenance predicates where compatible.
rejected_recommendations: Treating provenance existence as behavior or authenticity without verification
sources.limitations: An exact SLSA level is not adopted without release-platform authority and verification.

sources.title: SLSA build track and verification
verified_facts: The purpose of provenance is verification that artifacts were built as expected; expectations and trust roots matter.
binding_product_requirements: HCT-DISTRIBUTION must verify provenance/signatures against explicit trusted expectations, not merely parse or store them.
advisory_practices: Raise assurance as a release policy after build-platform ownership is decided.
rejected_recommendations: Claiming a SLSA level from an unsigned local metadata file
sources.limitations: Trust roots and builder identities are open release decisions.

sources.title: Cosign signature verification
verified_facts: Cosign can verify artifact signatures against keys or identity/issuer expectations.
advisory_practices: Use signing and identity-bound verification if the release authority adopts a signing service and policy.
rejected_recommendations: Making a signature substitute for reproducibility, installation, runtime, or product proof
sources.limitations: Signing identity, service, transparency policy, and offline verification are open decisions.

sources.title: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
verified_facts: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is a standardized timestamp input used to avoid current-time variability in reproducible outputs.
binding_product_requirements: Package creation uses an explicit source-derived timestamp or documents why bit-reproducibility is not achieved; stable order and metadata remain required.
advisory_practices: Normalize archive timestamps, ordering, permissions, locale, and paths.
rejected_recommendations: Embedding build-now timestamps in claim-bearing package bytes
sources.limitations: It is one reproducibility control, not a complete reproducible-build guarantee.

sources.title: git-worktree and git-status porcelain documentation
verified_facts: Git supports multiple linked worktrees; git worktree list --porcelain and git status --porcelain provide script-oriented state surfaces.
binding_product_requirements: The Ultra root recomputes live repository/worktree/dirty state with stable machine-readable Git commands before delegating or claiming.
advisory_practices: Use worktrees for isolated implementation branches and preserve per-worktree metadata.
rejected_recommendations: Trusting archived branch/status text as current
Assuming path isolation eliminates semantic conflicts
sources.limitations: The root must account for submodules, untracked/ignored files, and host-specific worktree behavior.

sources.title: Agent approvals and security
verified_facts: Codex exposes sandbox and approval controls; read-only mode is available; external workspace or network actions can require approval; project `.git`, `.agents`, and `.codex` paths are protected read-only under the documented workspace sandbox.
binding_product_requirements: Harness commands and agents declare effects structurally, keep read-only operations non-mutating, stop for external or destructive authority, and keep protected host configuration root-owned rather than leasing it to workers.
advisory_practices: Use least-privilege workspace-write or read-only modes and constrain network destinations when network is enabled.
rejected_recommendations: Assuming host sandboxing alone enforces Harness semantic ownership
Treating broad workspace-write as permission for external or destructive effects
sources.limitations: Actual sandbox, approval, connector annotations, and network policy must be observed in the live Codex project.

sources.title: Codex best practices
verified_facts: Project guidance should explain repository layout, run/build/test commands, engineering constraints, and what completion means.
binding_product_requirements: Repository fitting must produce concise, locally relevant guidance that a fresh agent can use without embedding the whole contract.
advisory_practices: Keep repository guidance practical, testable, and close to the applicable scope.
rejected_recommendations: Treating generated starter guidance as complete without repository-specific reconciliation
sources.limitations: Guidance quality and discovery must be behaviorally tested in the actual repository and host.
